terminalResult: For bounded operators on separable Hilbert spaces at interior upper-half-plane frequencies, support must be refined by spectral gap, Douglas coupling class, full complementability, convergence topology, Schatten ideal, approach net and scalarization. Ordinary, closed-range, factorized, topology-labelled-limit and refusal handlers exhaust the declared cases.

findings.statement: A common-scale factorization D=T^(1/2)Dhat T^(1/2), B=C T^(1/2) gives a bounded norm-holomorphic passive correction C Dhat^-1 C* without requiring closed range.
The Douglas square-root factorization, not kernel annihilation alone, is the bounded-response gate at non-closed range.
For T=diag(1/n), B=T^alpha: alpha<1/2 diverges, alpha=1/2 is bounded strong-only under ambient regularization, and alpha>1/2 is norm stable with compact residue.
Trace norm, norm, strong and weak operator convergence are strict, separately licensed layers even for positive residues.
Equal kernel and support projection do not determine closed range or the spectral gap.
Norm-convergent block endpoints can yield different strong Schur limits through sqrt(delta)L coupling on an emerging kernel.
An emerging kernel carries the whole bounded positive-operator residue cone R=LL*, modulo right-unitary coupling gauge.
No fixed finite probe compression plus trace reconstructs an unrestricted operator-valued residue.
Operator Harnack inequalities and Douglas factorization make the dissipative square-root range class invariant across compact frequency patches.
A bounded positive operator-valued Herglotz atom need not define a finite scalar trace measure or Fredholm determinant.
Fredholmness is not necessary: a non-Fredholm compact interior scale can still produce a bounded factorized or strong response.
The factorized theorem is frame covariant and does not require simultaneous diagonalization of T and Dhat.
